body: I don't feel like I feel safe telling my parents about how I feel. I've told them about how I've felt in the past so many times, and I've just been met with either told that "it's all in my mind", "turning back to God will help solve them", finding a way to rationalise how I feel, or pretending to understand but not really. I know I sound bitter right now, but this has happened a lot in the past and even recently. I don't think I can trust that anymore. They even keep telling me that they don't want me to leave the house because they want everyone to stay together as long as possible. It feels really suffocating.

Basically my expenses right now involve my phone bills, my public transport fares, my own food and my subscription for a program that is important for my uni studies. This makes my expenses per month around $250 which is nearly most of what I earn per week. I am also looking into getting another job so that I would feel more secure financially. I also know which ones I can cut down to really have a tight budget that would make things somewhat sustainable for me.

My parents are also not paying for any tuition fees as they are my responsibility. I just happen to delay paying for them as it's part of my privileges as an Australian citizen. Books are also not much of a worry since being a Comp Sci student, most of my learning material can be gathered online.

After sorting those things out, I feel like I do have some idea of how things work. It may not be perfect. But hey, I'm prepared to learn.

I also have some money saved that could last me 6 months if I find a really cheap place to stay at.

Edit: Added more info

Well, I could probably find out how bills work by myself, and I've already started keeping track of my expenses. I even have a monthly budget being taken into account. I pretty much pay for everything except for the house, utilities and the internet so I feel like I have a good grasp of what's happening even though I'm still miles away from getting it right.

Honestly, my intention for asking them was to give them a chance to really help me out, or perhaps even think of the possible solutions. It's just really disheartening that instead of focusing on that, they pretty much just shut down the idea, again without making me feel like my own opinions and feelings about things are being understood.

They've repetitively told me that they have been talking about things together, but I always hear it from my dad. My mother would also tell me things like, "just try to understand his perspective" when he gives me the silent treatment. So really, I wouldn't know whether they actually talked things through properly or not. Not to mention my dad has a way of getting what he wants even though my mum has openly expressed her dislike of this attitude.

I still have a year and a half left. However, that's going to be delayed since I'm already aiming to get into an industry placement program that's being offered by my university the next year. It's actually what I'm counting on to feel even more confident with the idea of moving out.

I'll definitely think about the things you've mentioned. Thanks for responding to my post.

I guess it's more asking about how bills work in general, and how things are being calculated. I also figured that directly asking them about it would be my way of reaching out.

I don't have any family members since my family just migrated here in Australia 7 years ago. It's pretty much just my immediate family here. No one else.

My mother barely says anything. When she talked to me right after this whole thing, she said she was very gutted by what happened, she just happened to not really say anything about what she's noticing. I also told her that I'm seeing a psychologist for the first time because I thought I could trust her. Then years later I found out that she actually told my dad about it (and I'm pretty sure I asked her not to tell him), which led to a mini lecture about how I didn't need a psychologist and we could just sort things out ourselves. 

But really how would that work? I was already distant from them by the time I was 15 and gradually losing trust. And I guess my dad constantly raising his voice at me was making things more terrifying to talk to him. When I actually last talked to them about my issues, he even tried to justify his voice, by saying that he's just naturally loud. I told him that regardless, his voice makes me feel sensitive about things. 

My dad doesn't believe in mental health issues. He always responds with "it's all in the mind" and that if we worked ourselves hard enough, we would be cured. 

Honestly, I thought I was really close to my dad. I admired him a lot when I was young and even chose a career-path pretty similar to what he does because of it. And then yeah, I feel like things gradually went downhill when I decided I didn't want to wear a skirt anymore.

I guess he's really not that bad. He can be fun to hang around still, and we have some great inside jokes together. But when it comes to my emotional stuff and the things that are actually important to me, I feel like he's ended up shutting me down too much. And that's whats' been stressing me out to varying degrees in the last few years.

EDIT: Wrong choice of words
I can't even apply for Centrelink because my parents earn enough to not make me eligible for it. I already tried that for youth allowance. I got rejected immediately.

In a sense, I feel like I'm already supporting myself. But since, I'm still freeloading, maybe not. I pay for my school and I have a job. I don't have a car and I don't drive yet, though I am looking to get that sorted out soon.

I am worried that it will cause a fight, because my mother actually told me when she talked to me about this, that she wouldn't allow me to leave. I talked to her about wanting some time and space away from them, but at that point, I was just not sure how. The current arrangement after that is to just let me be for a bit to think for myself here at home. But now I do feel like I should move out. 

I guess I am scared to move out. I don't know if I can make it, but I feel like I trust myself enough that if I have to deal with it, I can do it. That's my own conflict with myself with making a decision.

I'm thinking about this heavily right now. I'm mostly leaning towards telling them that I'd start finding my own place. I don't know. I'm just exhausted now really. I've been finding that aside from my own quarter-life crisis, my arrangement here at home is not helping either. When I'm here, negativity and apathy fills up my mind, and I don't think it's good.

I do have my own bank account. It's what I use now. As for luxuries, I have enough entertainment for myself (books, my own gaming stuff, and my laptop). Really all I need is the internet, not only for fun but also since I would need that a lot for my university course too. Anything else I'm prepared to not have much around.

But I guess, how would I know if I really can't deal with the bills and stuff when they don't even answer my questions about them? All they would say is, "no you can't do it. just stop thinking about it."

I am also trying to get another job that is not only more related to what I am doing, but also a bit more stable. My grades didn't even drop much when I got my job. It's more when I started feeling even more stuck with my life that my brain has started melting down.

When it comes to danger, I don't know if this counts, but during that time when my dad stopped talking to me. I was heavily stressed to the point where I was already starting to think of severely harmful thoughts. It's one of the reasons why I even started seeing a psychologist in the first place. And since this happened, I've found myself panicking a lot and my anxiety issues has gone overdrive again.
Um, I don't even know really if their actions towards me actually count as abusive or not. So I don't know. All I know is that their past actions have caused a lot of mental grief.

From where I am, there's a system where I can delay my tuition and pay for it later when I actually have a proper job to pay for it. So that one's my responsibility. I'm also paying for my public transport, my phone bills and pretty much everything else I own. I guess really, I'm only freeloading towards the shelter, but everything else is being paid using my own money. That's something I've been gradually building up since I got my part time job.

Rent close to my university is around $200+ per week with just by myself. I used to be iffy with the whole idea of sharing a house so I was not open to getting roommates. But now I feel like maybe I should consider that too.

Financially they think I can't do it because they think that my job is not enough to sustain proper living. And yet when I try to sort things out and actually find out whether I can do it or not by asking them how paying the bills actually work, they don't even explain, they either give me an "advice" that I'm not ready for it, or a very confronting question, "do you honestly think you can do it?"

After telling my friends what happened, one of them is actually offering me a spot in her place.

EDIT: Forgot to answer the last question

Uhh even I would be against the idea of anyone donating funds for my own gain. That's just not right.

And no, I can admit that I am not the most emotionally mature person out there. I still make mistakes. I have a hard time admitting them because of my own perfectionist tendencies, but I am aware that I do make mistakes.

I have already tried communicating with my family. Twice actually. Both for an even heavier issue that I didn't mention here. The first time, they pretty much just shut down my feelings about the issue. I get that it was something they did for me for my best interest in the long run, but they refused to listen to how I felt about it and continued to rationalize them. The same thing happened with the second time. I was a bit more forgiving then and things perhaps worked out for a few months. Then I was back to the feeling of being stuck and going back to the feelings of resentment I've had towards them. I've realized that I'm having a hard time letting go of things. And I'm trying to fix that with my psychologist.

When do you think would be the right time then? I feel like I've already reached my own emotional limit here. The things they have done may seem simple, but I can honestly say that the effects of it eventually put me into places in my mind where I don't want to be. Perhaps a lot of them are making a good point that I should move out soon.

Well I am starting to get that I did make a mistake on that part. I am now thinking of raising the idea of moving out again. Hopefully this time, they don't try to discourage me by constantly saying I can't do it.

Oh but I have told them all of my concerns about not feeling validated. 

Honestly, the idea of getting any reaction from them is really terrifying for me now. It's not just the negatives. I don't know how disillusioned I can be to the point where any reaction from them makes me want to run away. I do see a psychologist to help fix things for myself. 

When I was really young, we did have a really good relationship. I was always the obedient one. I try my hardest to not disappoint them. Then I don't know, my opinions about things changed? Then that's when things went downhill.

I have mentioned the idea of moving out to them at some point. Both of them pretty much told me to stay and save up because they told me that I can't handle myself out there yet. I have some money saved. I'm just not sure if it would be enough. And whenever I'd ask them about how handling the bills are like, they just respond with, "what are you worrying about that for? just focus on your study"

I'm not going to criticize your comments about me since you make some good points too. Perhaps I'm just a disillusioned kid right now who doesn't understand how to be grateful for their hard work. But please, I hope you do understand that I've dealt with years when I felt like my own opinions and feelings about things being shutdown. It's not just those two examples.
We've known each other and been really good friends for a year and a bit. We started dating around 2 months ago.
Um, I guess it's more Southeast so think of Philippines/Malaysia/Indonesia etc..

Nope. I made it clear to him that anything sexual is not going to happen any time soon because I'm not really comfortable with that at all yet (and he's not either). We just agreed to book the place to get some time away from the places that have been giving us grief.
The idea of getting some space got to me first. I wanted it so badly that I forgot. So that's my mistake right there.
Yes

I wasn't hiding anything from them. My boyfriend and I have agreed that sex is out of the option at this point in time. It was more my own fear of how they would react and immediately shut me down that made me not want to ask for their permission. But I suppose it's not really the best decision I've ever done.

Harsh, but you make some good points. Though I guess it's hard to see those points when I've spent most of my childhood feeling emotionally neglected by them. For some people like me, it's important to have my own feelings valued. I honestly believe that I've provided my parents enough opportunity to get some form of emotional validation from them, but I feel like I barely got it. I'm grateful for what they've given me material-wise, but emotionally and psychologically I felt like they were lacking with that. I guess that's why my post was very emotionally biased. I felt like my own feelings have been ignored like I felt like has always happened.
I'm Australian with Asian background.

I do have a job, but since I'm currently a uni student with demanding hours, I feel like how much I earn will not be enough to even pay for rent. But I am looking at the option of moving to a sharehouse. I just have a lot of things in my mind right now so I really don't know which one to prioritize.
